A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, table, equations, and Appendices A–J are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original experiments on phase retrieval, Life Expectancy distributionally robust optimization, and CIFAR10 training with ResNet18/50. Appendix A contains additional empirical ablations.

after.justification: Section 7 retains the original experimental comparisons, and Appendix A reports ablations including revised batch-size convergence results in Figure 9.

M1.justification: The AN-GD update and IAN-SGD estimator, independent sampling, adaptive normalization, and clipping mechanism remain unchanged in Equations 6 and 12–14. Revisions concern theoretical guarantees and experimental documentation.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic phase retrieval, Life Expectancy regression for DRO, and CIFAR10 with ResNet18/50. The appendix retains the same tasks and batch-size scenarios; no dataset or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain their baseline memberships, including SPIDER for phase retrieval/DRO and Adam and Adagrad for neural-network training. Figures 2–4 and 10 retain the same comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 replaces the identical five-entry learning-rate lists previously given for both tasks with distinct six-entry lists matching the six retained batch sizes. Figure 9 also reports DRO trajectories through 6,000 rather than 10,000 samples. Main benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 revises the evidence testing IAN-SGD convergence with small, equal gradient and normalization batches by replacing both Figure 9 trajectories. The other normalization, independent-batch-size, stabilization, and noise-parameter analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the fixed-seed initialization statement for neural-network experiments. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 9 reports different convergence trajectories. In phase retrieval, batch size 16 crosses objective value 100 before batch size 8 in v2; this ordering reverses in v3. The DRO curves also change. These are replacement results under revised learning rates, rather than evidence of a same-setting performance gain. Other empirical plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and Appendix E revise the initial-gap dependence and local-convergence constants. Lemma 3 and Appendix J correct a step-size factor from 2τ1+1 to 2τ1+2 and repair associated inequalities. Appendix C revises the phase-retrieval gradient, finite-sum scaling, and smoothness constants. These refine existing derivations without adding theorems or changing the headline asymptotic rates.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: explaining adaptive normalization under generalized PŁ geometry and achieving O(ε−4) stochastic sample complexity through IAN-SGD under relaxed noise assumptions.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 adds a substantive comparison between the per-sample affine noise assumption and variance-based assumptions. New Remark 3 explains the tradeoff between batch size and sample complexity and identifies optimizing that tradeoff for IAN-SGD as future work.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-access link in the abstract footnote and newly states that the DRO primal and dual variables are optimized in parallel. Appendix A.4 also supplies complete task-specific learning-rate mappings. These improve documentation; the PDFs alone do not verify the linked resource's availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Table 1 revise the characterization of Koloskova et al. from convergence to a noise-dependent neighborhood to ε-stationarity with O(ε−5) complexity under specified parameter choices. V3 also adds references for Kaiming initialization and PyTorch. Consolidating duplicate Koloskova references does not remove a distinct work.

P1.justification: V3 makes grammatical and terminology edits, expands the notation summary and noise-assumption discussion, adds detailed affiliations, and introduces acknowledgements. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 9 is redrawn, including a shorter DRO horizontal range, and Table 1's caption is revised. Expanded front matter and removal of the preprint header cause text and figure reflow. The overall layout and figure/table inventory are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 repairs several algebraic inconsistencies, resolves the incomplete learning-rate mappings in Appendix A.4, and adds useful implementation and code-access information. These changes improve technical clarity and reproducibility. The central methods and main experimental evidence remain stable, so the overall improvement is limited.
